Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 103, verses 1–3:

﴿By Time (al-ʿAṣr)﴾ Concerning this there are three opinions. The first is that it refers to the afternoon prayer (ṣalat al-ʿaṣr), by which God swears because of its excellence. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever misses the afternoon prayer, it is as if he has been robbed of his family and his property." The second is that it refers to the late part of the day (al-ʿashiyy), by which He swears just as He swears by the forenoon (al-ḍuḥā). This is supported by the statement of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb: "I asked the Messenger of God (ﷺ) about al-ʿaṣr, and he said: 'Your Lord swears by the end of the day.'" The third is that it refers to time in general.

﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss﴾ "Mankind" (al-insān) is a genus noun, and for this reason He excepted from it those who believe; so the exception is a connected exception (istithnāʾ muttaṣil).

﴿And they advise one another to truth﴾ That is, they enjoin one another to the truth and to patience. The truth is Islam and what it contains. Within this there is an indication of the falsehood of the disbelievers, and in patience there is an indication of the patience of the believers under the harm the disbelievers inflicted upon them in Mecca.
